description: Verdict meta-vectors for the grading language (docs/contract/grading.md): (label, entry, file, actual, claims_cost) -> the verdict, as santa_check::grading::Verdict::to_json writes it (graded dimensions only; a null actual is a missing one). An interpreter of vectors/grading.json is conformant iff it reproduces every verdict. Carried over from the per-tier oracle files, plus nipopow.

cases.name: transaction/accept-cost-unclaimed
cases.description: A runner that does not claim the cost dimension (manifest cost:false): cost is not graded, whatever it answers.
cases.label: transaction

cases.name: transaction/accept-cost-null-while-claimed-is-coal
cases.description: A runner that claims the cost dimension and answers cost:null on an accepted spend is cost-not-implemented: coal on the cost dimension, as on the eval tier.
cases.label: transaction

cases.name: transaction/accept-expected-cost-null-is-na
cases.description: A value-only vector (expected.cost null): cost is not graded, even for a runner that claims it.
cases.label: transaction

cases.name: transaction/reject-errored-coal
cases.description: BY DESIGN: errored on a reject vector is coal, not a clean rejection. The tx tier explicitly separates clean-reject (valid:false, error:null) from failed-verdict (error:errored, valid:null). Differs from the eval reject arm where errored IS the clean reject.
cases.label: transaction

cases.name: block/accept-all-nice
cases.description: Accept vector: valid:true, post_digest matches, cost matches -> all three dims nice.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/accept-valid-coal
cases.description: Accept vector: conformer returned valid:false — valid dim is coal, post_digest and cost both n/a.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/accept-digest-coal
cases.description: Accept vector: valid nice, but post_digest mismatch -> digest coal, cost n/a (digest failed).
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/accept-cost-coal
cases.description: Accept vector: valid nice, post_digest matches, cost mismatch -> cost coal.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/accept-cost-unclaimed
cases.description: Accept vector, a runner that does not claim the cost dimension (manifest cost:false): cost n/a, whatever it answers.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/accept-cost-null-while-claimed-is-coal
cases.description: Accept vector, valid and post_digest nice, a runner that claims the cost dimension answers cost:null -> cost-not-implemented: cost coal, as on the eval tier.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/reject-nice
cases.description: Reject vector: expected valid:false, actual valid:false error:null -> valid nice, post_digest n/a, cost n/a.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/reject-errored-coal
cases.description: BY DESIGN: errored on a reject vector is coal, not a clean rejection. Block tier mirrors tx tier: clean-reject = valid:false error:null; failed-verdict = error:errored valid:null.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/not-implemented
cases.description: Not-implemented: coverage verdict, not coal.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/panicked
cases.description: Panicked actual: coal unconditionally before any expected check.
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/panicked-on-reject-still-coal
cases.description: Panicked on a reject vector: coal unconditionally (a crash is not a clean rejection).
cases.label: block

cases.name: block/exceeded-on-accept-is-coal

cases.name: block/exceeded-on-reject-is-coal-not-nice
cases.description: A budget hit on a reject vector is not a clean rejection.
cases.label: block

cases.name: chain/voting-reject-errored-nice

cases.name: chain/voting-reject-panicked-coal

cases.label: chain

cases.name: chain/gate-valid-mismatch-coal

cases.name: chain/gate-reject-errored-nice

cases.label: chain

cases.name: chain/gate-reject-clean-prohibition-coal
cases.description: fork_vote_gate reject vector: a conformer folding the missing-121 throw into valid:false is consensus-equivalent in-band but red by design (contract S2 - the split pins mechanics finer than the JVM observable).
cases.label: chain

cases.name: authds/prove-both-nice
cases.description: avl_prove: proofs and digests both match expected exactly, error null → proof nice, digest nice.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/prove-proof-coal-digest-nice
cases.description: avl_prove: the proof bytes diverge from the canonical proof (a non-canonical serialization) while the resulting digest still matches expected. proof and digest are independent — the digest match must not suppress the proof mismatch, because a digest-correct/proof-wrong runner is precisely the defect class (non-canonical AVL proof bytes) this tier exists to catch.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/prove-both-coal-data-mismatch
cases.description: avl_prove: both the proof bytes and the digest diverge from expected → both dimensions grade coal, independently of each other.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/prove-errored-coal
cases.description: avl_prove: the runner reports an error even though the proof and digest values it produced happen to match expected byte-for-byte (stale data from a previous entry, or a partially populated actual). A non-null error must veto both dimensions regardless of value equality — a failed run is never gradeable as nice.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-full-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: the proof is accepted as expected, every operation result matches, and the resulting digest matches → all three dimensions nice.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-over-accept-coal
cases.description: avl_verify: the reference verifier refuses this proof (proof_accepted:false) but the runner anchors it anyway (proof_accepted:true) — an over-accept, the failure mode the reject arm exists to catch. accepted grades coal, and there is nothing legitimate downstream to grade, so results and digest are n/a rather than compared against data the reference never produced.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-rejected-proof-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: both the reference and the runner refuse the proof at the same starting digest under the same settings. Reproducing a rejection is itself a nice verdict; results and digest are n/a because no operations were legitimately attempted on either side.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-results-mismatch-suppresses-digest
cases.description: avl_verify: the proof is accepted on both sides, but one operation's outcome differs (ok:true vs ok:false) → results grades coal. digest is downstream of the operations, not parallel to them, so it is suppressed to n/a rather than compared — a digest computed after a divergent operation sequence carries no information.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-digest-mismatch-alone-is-coal
cases.description: avl_verify: proof_accepted matches and every operation result matches, but the final digest differs from expected — the realistic shape of a subtly-broken AVL implementation that reproduces every individual operation correctly yet computes the wrong final root. digest grades coal on its own merits; accepted and results are unaffected, because a wrong root does not retroactively invalidate operations that were themselves reproduced correctly.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/verify-poisoned-null-digest-nice
cases.description: avl_verify: a failing operation poisons the verifier so it reports no digest — new_digest_hex:null is a real, meaningful value here, not an absent field. Both sides poisoned identically is a correctly reproduced verdict, so digest grades nice via null-equals-null, not n/a and not coal.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/panicked
cases.description: A runner crash grades panicked unconditionally, before the entry's kind or expected values are even consulted — checked ahead of every other precedence rule.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/not-implemented
cases.description: A conformer with no prover declares not-implemented rather than attempting the operation. This is a coverage/growth-ledger cell, not a coal verdict — checked after panicked but before any value grading.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/unknown-kind-coal
cases.description: An entry kind this grader does not recognize (a future or malformed kind discriminator) must never silently pass — it grades coal on every dimension of the default authds_prove shape rather than defaulting to nice.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/exceeded-on-accept-is-coal
cases.description: A bounded file over its budget (the tier-neutral exceeded actual): coal unconditionally before any expected check.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: authds/exceeded-on-reject-is-coal-not-nice
cases.description: A budget hit where the proof is rejected is not a clean rejection.
cases.label: authds

cases.name: block/valid-accept-without-post-digest-is-post-digest-red
cases.description: A valid block whose expected and actual post_digest are both absent: the digest dimension needs two non-null digests, so it is red (and cost, after it, not graded). Schema-unreachable for a validated vector; the rule is the contract's.
cases.label: block

cases.name: nipopow/interlinks-without-chain-or-interlinks-is-red
cases.description: No file chain and no interlinks in the actual: nothing to compare is red, never nice by null equals null.
cases.label: nipopow

cases.label: nipopow

cases.name: wire/expected-bytes-present-but-null-is-red
cases.description: expected_bytes_hex present (even null) is the expected side: first takes the first present key, as the legacy grade did; a null expectation fails the case-insensitive comparison.
cases.label: wire

cases.description: header_votes: the verdict equals the expected one (valid).
cases.label: chain

cases.name: chain/header-votes-valid-false-nice

cases.label: chain

cases.name: eval/expected-errored-missing-actual-is-reject-red

cases.label: eval

cases.name: chain/retargeting-nbits-as-float-nice
cases.description: Numbers compare numerically: an nbits answered as 84150434.0 is the expected 84150434 (a deliberate difference from the hard-coded grade, which compared JSON values exactly).
